summary.text: John Clemmons is the Democratic state representative for Tennessee House District 55, part of Davidson County in Nashville, a seat he has held since November 2014, and he is the incumbent on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.
He is an attorney and mediator.

paragraphs.text: Clemmons earned a B.A. in history from Columbia University in 1999 and a J.D. from the University of Memphis Law School in 2006.
The legislature's biography lists him as an attorney and mediator.
Before joining the House he served on the Tennessee Civil Service Commission from 2009 to 2012 and on the Metropolitan Board of Fair Commissioners from 2012 to 2014.
Clemmons has been a member of the House since the 109th General Assembly and chaired the House Democratic Caucus during the 113th General Assembly.
The House website lists him as a member of the Calendar & Rules and Government Operations committees and the Joint Judiciary and Government committee.
Ballotpedia reports that he advanced from the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary and will face Republican Jayla Thomas in the general election.
His community involvement includes service on the board of directors of Silent No Longer Tennessee since 2022 and on the board of Friends of Sevier Park since 2013.
